title: RuntimeDecision
description: PROPOSED, NOT ADMITTED. Separates what the grounds establish (epistemic_status), what the runtime did (execution_disposition), and why it did it (decision_basis). schemas/draft/runtime-evaluation.schema.json collapses all three into a single `verdict` field; that collapse is the defect this schema exists to correct. The cross-field constraints in `allOf` are the contract, not documentation: a decision violating one is invalid, not merely discouraged. See adr/ADR-013.md. schemas/draft is NOT modified by this proposal.

reason_code.description: Stable machine-readable reason. Registry in docs/contracts/WARRANT-CONTRACT-v0.1.md.

control_policy_reason_code.$comment: Reason codes that justify a CONTROL_REQUIREMENT basis.

overlay_id.description: A warrant-policy rule (WP-n) or decision-mode overlay (DM-n) identifier from the canonical mapping.

epistemic_status.description: What the admitted grounds establish about the claim. ESTABLISHED: the grounds establish it independently of any unresolved ground, under the profile's hereditary contract. CONDITIONALLY_SUPPORTED: the current admitted marking supports the claim, but the positive result depends on one or more unverified grounds and is not invariant under admissible refinement. REFUTED: the grounds establish its negation. UNRESOLVED: the grounds do not settle it, or it was never validly evaluated. CONTRADICTED: the admitted ground set is inconsistent, which is a finding about the grounds rather than a refutation of the proposition. ON CREDIT MUST NEVER serialise as ESTABLISHED: that would authorise action on an unverified link. Nor may it collapse to UNRESOLVED merely because grounds are unverified, which would discard a real positive result.

execution_disposition.description: What the runtime did. Independent of epistemic_status: a BLOCK may accompany UNRESOLVED (fail closed) or REFUTED (grounds establish the negation), and those are not the same event.

decision_basis.description: Why the runtime did it. SUBSTANTIVE: the admitted grounds determine a positive, negative, or contradictory epistemic result. PRECAUTIONARY: the grounds remain unresolved and the runtime fails closed. PROCEDURAL: the claim could not be validly evaluated because an artifact, binding, version, availability, or integrity precondition failed. CONTROL_REQUIREMENT: the claim WAS validly evaluated, but the admitted control requires a particular assurance grade, human role, escalation path, or non-automatic decision mode. Only SUBSTANTIVE is a finding about the world; PRECAUTIONARY, PROCEDURAL and CONTROL_REQUIREMENT are never findings that the proposition is false.

reason_codes.description: Sorted lexicographically, deterministic. At least one is always present, including on ALLOW.

missing_ground_ids.description: Level 1: stable proposition or atom identifiers as emitted by the kernel. Present whenever the kernel reported unverified grounds, INCLUDING when the outcome is ALLOW.

missing_ground_anchors.description: Level 2: human-review references linking each missing proposition to its source and admission context. Enrichment is the OIC adapter's job, never the kernel's. An empty list means enrichment has not run; it does not mean there are no missing grounds.

warrant_artifact_id.description: The warrant this decision rests on, or null when no usable warrant existed. Null with ALLOW is forbidden by the constraints below.

warrant_state.description: Why the warrant was or was not usable. MISBOUND covers epoch, formula, profile, source-version and admission-version mismatch. UNSUPPORTED_GRADE means the grade VOCABULARY is unknown. UNSUPPORTED_RESULT means the vocabulary is known but the disposition/grade/raw-verdict/unverified COMBINATION violates the frozen profile - an invalid combination is never reported as a grade defect. NOT_REQUIRED applies only when the control explicitly declared not_required or not_applicable, and never waives authority, admission, evidence or version checks.

warranty_grade_observed.description: Grade the warrant actually carried. Null only when no warrant was evaluated.

warranty_grade_required.description: Minimum grade the control's warrant_requirement declares. Null only when warrant_requirement.mode is not_required or not_applicable. There is no default: an absent requirement is a contract error, not a permissive one.

on_unknown_applied.description: The envelope's on_unknown policy, set ONLY when it was the reason for the outcome, otherwise null. `deny` means an operational fail-closed block and is never evidence that the proposition is false; the constraints below forbid pairing it with SUBSTANTIVE or ALLOW.

replay_reference.description: How to replay this decision to its exact control, admission, sources, warrant, inputs, and versions (I-15). REQUIRED and non-empty on EVERY decision including failures: an evaluation that blocked because no warrant existed must still be replayable, or the failure cannot be audited.

unverified_ground_policy_applied.description: The control's unverified_ground_policy, recorded when it determined the outcome, otherwise null. Permission to act on conditional support is an admitted control decision, not a stronger epistemic claim, so the policy that granted it stays on the record.

applied_control_overlay_ids.description: Stage-2 and stage-3 identifiers that changed the outcome, in deterministic order (warrant-policy rules before decision-mode overlays). Empty when none applied. The identity overlay DM-1 (decision_mode automatic) is never recorded. Every matched policy reason code is retained in reason_codes even when a later stage changes the final execution disposition, so the lineage of a decision survives.

warrant_requirement_mode.description: The mode the control declared. Null ONLY when the control contract itself was missing or invalid (OIC-W-0026), which is a procedural contract error. An explicit not_required or not_applicable is a declaration and is recorded as such - it is never conflated with an absent one.

conditional_support_subscription_referen.description: Binds the unresolved grounds of a conditional ALLOW to a deterministic recomputation subscription. Non-null and non-empty whenever CONDITIONALLY_SUPPORTED reaches ALLOW: acting on a result that rides an unverified link is only defensible if the system will be told when that link moves. Null on every other route. A subscription is plumbing, never evidence of stronger epistemic support. The VEIP carrier is deferred; this field preserves the binding for that later contract.

conditional_support_subscription_ground_.description: Grounds the subscription covers, in deterministic order. For a conditional ALLOW this must equal missing_ground_ids exactly: a subscription that covers only some of the load-bearing grounds leaves the rest able to move unnoticed.

conditional_support_subscription_trigger.description: Events that must trigger recomputation, in deterministic order. All five are required for a conditional ALLOW. Verification, expiry, revocation, correction and a relevant epoch change can each falsify the result, so omitting any one leaves a path by which the ALLOW silently outlives its grounds.

allOf.$comment: Rule 1. ALLOW has exactly two positive routes. Common preconditions apply to both.

oneOf.$comment: Route A - EARNED / hereditary. missing_ground_ids may be NON-EMPTY: measured, 61 of 294 census cases carry unverified atoms that are irrelevant to a hereditary conclusion. They are preserved, and they do not weaken ESTABLISHED.
Route B - ON CREDIT / sound, accepted by explicit control policy.

allOf.$comment: Rule 2. UNRESOLVED can neither ALLOW nor claim a substantive finding.
Rule 3. CONDITIONALLY_SUPPORTED: never substantive, never without missing grounds, never with an on_unknown fallback.

Rule 4. CONDITIONALLY_SUPPORTED + until-verification: never ALLOW, always PRECAUTIONARY, always OIC-W-0025. v0.1 does not model risk, reversibility, compensation or recovery controls sufficient to permit automatic consequential ALLOW here.

Rule 5. Stage-2 outcomes for CONDITIONALLY_SUPPORTED + sound, when no decision-mode overlay applied. forbid must BLOCK and escalate must ESCALATE; a later stage-3 overlay may still redirect, which is why this is conditioned on DM-2/DM-3 being absent.
Rule 6. Same, for the escalate policy.
Rule 7. REFUTED never permits the action; an overlay may redirect it while preserving the status.
Rule 8. CONTRADICTED behaves like REFUTED for execution.
Rule 9. Any non-USABLE warrant state cannot ALLOW.
Rule 10. A non-null on_unknown fallback means the epistemic state was unresolved. It cannot ALLOW and cannot be substantive.
Rule 11. An unverified-ground policy is only meaningful for conditional support.
Rule 12. CONTROL_REQUIREMENT must carry a control-policy reason code and at least one overlay identifier explaining which stage produced it.
Rule 13. A null warrant_requirement_mode means the control contract was missing or invalid, which is a procedural error and never permits the action.
Rule 14. An explicit non-requirement is recorded as NOT_REQUIRED with OIC-W-0024, and has no ALLOW path in v0.1.
Rule 15. A subscription reference is only meaningful for conditional support, and any subscription that exists must cover at least one ground.
